brief.topic: A Quiet Clock Hidden in a Length

s01: A small weight swings, and finds its way back.
Its rhythm comes mostly from length, not heaviness.
Imagine a tiny bob on a light, unstretching string.
We keep the swings small and leave friction aside.
The distance runs from the pivot to the center of the bob.
Gravity pulls the bob toward the lowest point.
A longer pendulum turns through its angle more slowly.
The time for a full cycle grows with the square root of length.
Here are two strings, one four times as long.
Release them from the same small angle.
While the long one completes one cycle, the short one completes two.
Their masses do not enter this ideal period rule.
Now compare lengths of one and nine.
The longer pendulum takes three times as long for a cycle.
These are small-angle approximations, not rules for a huge swing.
A quiet clock can be hidden in a distance.

scenes.narration:
A small weight swings, and finds its way back. Its rhythm comes mostly from length, not heaviness.

Imagine a tiny bob on a light, unstretching string. We keep the swings small and leave friction aside. The distance runs from the pivot to the center of the bob.

Gravity pulls the bob toward the lowest point. A longer pendulum turns through its angle more slowly. The time for a full cycle grows with the square root of length.

Here are two strings, one four times as long. Release them from the same small angle. While the long one completes one cycle, the short one completes two. Their masses do not enter this ideal period rule.

Now compare lengths of one and nine. The longer pendulum takes three times as long for a cycle. These are small-angle approximations, not rules for a huge swing. A quiet clock can be hidden in a distance.
